rawInput.answer: In compose.ts's dispatch(i), each handler call is wrapped in try/catch: if a thrown value is `instanceof Error` and an `onError` handler was supplied, it sets `context.error = err` and calls `onError(err, context)`, assigning the result to `context.res` (this overwrite happens even if the context was already finalized, since the assignment condition is `finalized === false || isError`); non-Error throws, or errors when no onError is supplied, simply rethrow up the call stack. hono-base.ts wires this up by calling `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`, where `this.errorHandler` defaults to a handler that special-cases `HTTPException`-like errors (checks `'getResponse' in err`) or falls back to logging + a generic 500, and can be overridden per-app via `app.onError()`; anything that escapes compose (e.g. a rethrown non-Error, or the error handler itself throwing) is caught by the outer try/catch in `#dispatch`, which calls `#handleError` once more (re-invoking `this.errorHandler` for Error instances, or rethrowing non-Errors out of `fetch()` entirely). The single-handler fast path in `#dispatch` bypasses compose and applies the same try/catch + `.catch()` pattern directly around the lone handler, and `.route()` isolates a sub-app's own error handler by wrapping its handler in `compose([], app.errorHandler)` so nested app errors are handled before propagating to the parent app's handler.

report.answer: In compose.ts's dispatch(i), each handler call is wrapped in try/catch: if a thrown value is `instanceof Error` and an `onError` handler was supplied, it sets `context.error = err` and calls `onError(err, context)`, assigning the result to `context.res` (this overwrite happens even if the context was already finalized, since the assignment condition is `finalized === false || isError`); non-Error throws, or errors when no onError is supplied, simply rethrow up the call stack. hono-base.ts wires this up by calling `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`, where `this.errorHandler` defaults to a handler that special-cases `HTTPException`-like errors (checks `'getResponse' in err`) or falls back to logging + a generic 500, and can be overridden per-app via `app.onError()`; anything that escapes compose (e.g. a rethrown non-Error, or the error handler itself throwing) is caught by the outer try/catch in `#dispatch`, which calls `#handleError` once more (re-invoking `this.errorHandler` for Error instances, or rethrowing non-Errors out of `fetch()` entirely). The single-handler fast path in `#dispatch` bypasses compose and applies the same try/catch + `.catch()` pattern directly around the lone handler, and `.route()` isolates a sub-app's own error handler by wrapping its handler in `compose([], app.errorHandler)` so nested app errors are handled before propagating to the parent app's handler.
